subject: LumenX-small transient 5xx surge — customer communications and recovery timeline
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@skyline.health>, PlatformOps <ops@skyline.health>
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: LumenX-small — transient 5xx spike observed (initial notice)

Alex / PlatformOps team,

I wanted to let you know we detected an elevated rate of 502/504 responses coming from the LumenX-small serving pool that powers your inference endpoint (skyline-prod/us-west-2). The spike began at ~08:58 PST and peaked around 09:05 PST; we've been triaging and I wanted to share what we know now and the immediate actions we're taking.

What we observed:
- 502/504 rate rose from baseline (~0.1%) to ~3.8% over a 7-minute window.
- P95 latency increased from 220ms to ~1.6s for the affected requests.
- Errors were concentrated on requests with long prompt histories (>2k tokens) and streaming sessions.

Initial mitigations (in flight):
1) We’ve temporarily routed new requests to an expanded LumenX-medium fallback pool for your config (this preserves latency for most requests).
2) We’re throttling concurrent KV cache reuse for long-lived sessions to avoid large in-GPU KV growth while we debug.
3) Ops has rolled a conservative kernel/alloc fallback to prevent transient OOMs on the small instance class.

Next steps and ask from your side:
- Can you confirm whether any jobs from your side were running long-history batch syntheses at ~08:50-09:10 PST? That would help validate the long-history hypothesis.
- We’ll follow up with a postmortem and a timeline by EOD PST.

Attachments: obs-summary-20261220.csv (short telemetry extract).

Apologies for the disruption — I’ll post updates here as we have them.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
--
Attachment: obs-summary-20261220.csv (CSV telemetry sample, 3MB)
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@skyline.health>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: PlatformOps <ops@skyline.health>
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 09:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: LumenX-small — transient 5xx spike observed (initial notice)

Thanks for the quick heads-up, Ben.

We did have a scheduled nightly patient-synthesis job that hit around 08:52 PST (long prompts, multi-turn), but it’s uncommon for it to be that dense. PlatformOps is checking their side for any retries that could have piled on.

Impact: a small subset of background workflows received 5xx and auto-retried; user-facing pages experienced degraded responses for ~3-4 minutes. Not a full outage but enough to surface errors in our logs and a few support tickets.

Please keep us posted on the postmortem — we’ll hold off on any large replays until we get guidance.

—Alex
Alex Turner
SRE Lead, Skyline Health
alex.turner@skyline.health
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: LumenX-small spike — immediate ops/comms plan

Team — quick sync notes from the triage window.

Summary:
- Root cause appears to be a combination of KV cache growth + a new micro-quant kernel that regressed under long-sequence streaming workloads on the small instance class. That kernel path is in our canary experiment (rolled 2026-12-19 23:40 UTC).
- The expanded fallback to LumenX-medium has reduced customer-facing errors but at a higher cost footprint.

Action items (assigned):
- Marissa: draft a customer-facing timeline + RCA; include mitigation steps and next steps. Target: initial draft by 16:00 PST. (see postmortem-draft-20261220.md)
- Karthik: roll the kernel experiment back and publish rollback SHA to RW-INC-1987. Estimate 20 minutes to complete and validate.
- Stephanie: prepare a credit/comp plan if Skyline reports >0.5% error rate for the hour; coordinate with Finance.

Notes on comms tone: be explicit about the canary experiment and the rollback. We want to avoid vague language — customers appreciate clear technical explanations here.

Ben
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, Alex Turner <alex.turner@skyline.health>
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: RE: LumenX-small — post-incident update and preliminary RCA

Alex / team,

Thank you for the patience — here is our preliminary timeline and findings. Full postmortem doc is attached (postmortem-draft-20261220.md).

Timeline (UTC):
- 2026-12-20T16:58:00Z: Canary kernel v2.3.7 rolled for LumenX-small in us-west-2.
- 2026-12-20T16:52:00Z: Increased long-history traffic observed from multiple tenants (including Skyline scheduled job).
- 2026-12-20T17:05:00Z: Error rate spike detected; we automatically routed to fallback pools and started rollback.
- 2026-12-20T17:22:00Z: Kernel rollback completed; error rate trended back to baseline by 17:34:00Z.

Preliminary root cause:
1) Regression in a new micro-quantization kernel path (v2.3.7) that interacts poorly with large KV cache allocations during streaming long-history sessions, causing transient allocation failures that surfaced as 502/504.
2) The canary rollout targeted a small fraction of small-class instances but coincided with high long-history workload, amplifying the impact.

Mitigations applied:
- Immediate rollback of v2.3.7 for small-class (completed 17:22Z).
- Throttling of KV reuse for sessions exceeding 2k tokens (temporary safeguard).
- For Skyline specifically we routed live traffic to LumenX-medium (lower error rate) while rollback was validated.

Next steps / commitments:
- We will perform a full regression test matrix for the micro-quant kernel across long-history streaming scenarios and publish results by 2026-12-23.
- We will provide an itemized credit for Skyline’s impacted window (per Stephanie/Finance).
- Follow-up Postmortem (final) and a recommended mitigation plan (config guardrail + improved canary heuristics) by 2026-12-22 EOD PST.

Attachment: postmortem-draft-20261220.md (draft).

Alex — any impact details you can share (number of user-facing tickets, rough % of background jobs retried) will help quantify the credit.

Thanks,
Marissa
Sr. Reliability PM, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@skyline.health>, PlatformOps <ops@skyline.health>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 18:34:00 -0800
Subject: Final update: LumenX-small — recovery confirmed and next steps

Alex / PlatformOps,

Quick final note now that we’ve validated the rollback and run 60+ minutes of steady-state checks.

What we did:
- Rolled back problematic kernel (v2.3.7) from all small-class serving nodes at 17:22Z.
- Validated baseline error rates and P95 latency returned to normal by 17:34Z.
- Applied temporary KV-reuse guardrail for >2k token sessions for the next 48 hours while we complete regression testing.

What to expect next:
- Final postmortem and suggested guardrails delivered by 2026-12-22 EOD PST.
- Itemized credit spreadsheet for the impacted window shared by 2026-12-21 (Stephanie / Finance will lead).
- Permanent canary-heuristic change to avoid small-class exposure during long-history traffic (target mid-Jan release).

We’re sorry for the disruption — thank you for the quick notes on your side which helped accelerate validation. If you’d like a short post-incident call tomorrow to walk through the timeline, happy to set that up.

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
